text:
Maya K: quick thread - prototyping the "edge-judger" concept but want a robust way to revoke or rotate policies quickly without touching every router deployment. ideas?
Drew H: we should treat policy blobs like certs + CRL. sign them, give them TTL, and push a compact revocation list (PRL) that edge agents poll.
Priya S: agree. important: revocation must be fast (seconds) for bad fallback decisions. polling every 30s might be too slow for high-severity incidents.
Maya K: proposal: hybrid push/pull. control-plane pushes an immediate revocation push via a fanout channel (kafka/ctrl-plane-notify) + edges fall back to PRL if push missed.
Drew H: format sketch (compact JSON):
```
{
  "policy_id": "p-2026-03-23-01",
  "issued_at": 1775001200,
  "expires_at": 1775087600,
  "signer_kid": "cp-rot1",
  "rules": [
    {"route_prefix": "/chat/v1/", "fallback": "model-legacy", "tenant_overrides": ["acct:bigbank"]}
  ]
}
```
Priya S: and PRL example: ["p-2026-03-23-01", "p-2026-03-22-09"] — edges check local cache and refuse revoked ones.
Maya K: security: store CP signing keys in KMS/HSM, rotate weekly. edges only need public KID/thumbprint to verify.
Drew H: ops question: who initiates emergency revoke? on-call can hit an API that both pushes revocation and opens an incident. good to tie to runbook automation (auto-revokes on certain metric thresholds).
Priya S: yes — automatically revoke if model-quality delta > X and 500-rate spikes concurrently. but auto-revoke needs manual confirmation path for ambiguous signals.
Maya K: metrics and observability: emit judger.policy_applied, judger.policy_revoked, judger.reconcile_latency, judger.fallback_reason (enum). trace spans should include policy_id and decision_version.
Drew H: we need a reconciliation loop: edge agent should reconcile every T (default 15s) and attempt to re-fetch blobs when PRL is updated. also backoff on network errors.
Priya S: for tenants: include cohort tags in rules so edges can make per-tenant picks without full control-plane round trips. e.g., "cohort:beta, cohort:enterprise".
Maya K: runbook snippet for emergency revoke:
- on-call triggers /control-plane/revoke -> fanout push + record incident id
- edges receive push and switch to safe-fallback-mode (route only to verified fallbacks)
- control-plane creates short-lived safe-policy for edges to use while team investigates
- if edges fail to receive push after 10s, PRL poll forces revoke
OpsBot: note: ensure audit logs include revoker identity + incident id. we should also emit alert to #oncall when a revoke push occurs.
Drew H: performance: policy blobs must be tiny. avoid full routing tables. just include route_prefix hashes + fallback ids. use base64 signed payloads.
Priya S: testing: we should add chaos tests that drop push messages to simulate partial revocation and verify PRL reconciliation covers it.
Maya K: UX: provide a "dry-run revoke" mode where edges report what they'd revoke but don't switch traffic. useful during drills.
Drew H: one more: TTL semantics. if an edge is offline past policy expiry, it should fall back to control-plane-defaults (deny auto-fallback) to avoid stale aggressive fallbacks.
Priya S: agreed. default behavior: expired policies => passive mode only until reconcilation.
Maya K: action items: Drew -> implement PRL prototype + push channel; Priya -> metrics + chaos tests; I'll draft the RFC addendum with runbook + HSM key rotation notes.
Drew H: ack, prototype by next Wed.
Priya S: will add dashboard + alert rules to ops playbook.
CanaryBot: policy_push: p-2026-03-23-01 pushed to 12/12 edge agents at 1775001260
Maya K: thanks all, this should let us kill bad fallbacks fast without a heavy control-plane dependency :)
